This government appeal on behalf of the State along with application for grant of leave has been
filed challenging the acquittal of accused-Mukesh in Special Session Trial No.1334 of 2019 (State
Versus Mukesh) arising out of Case Crime No.126 of 2019 under Sections 363, 366, 376(3) I.P.C.
and 3/4 of The Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police Station Civil Line,
District Budaun.

entities.text: Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act, 2012

sentences.text: 2.  As per the prosecution case, the informant's daughter aged about 16 years has been enticed by the accused on 07.02.2019 at 11.00 a.m.
The informant, his wife and son had gone to the relatives place and the victim was alone at home.
The informant has also alleged that one Geeta, who is his neighbour, has also helped the accused in elopement of the victim.

On the basis of such allegations,

sentences.text: It may be noticed, at this stage, that the victim remained with the accused for almost three months and ultimately she has been recovered on 18th of May, 2019.
In the medical examination of the victim, no external or internal injuries have been found on her.

3. The victim in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. alleged that she had joined the company of accused on her own volition, but at the subsequent stage of trial, she has taken a different stand, as per which she was enticed by the accused and forced to live in his company.
4. So far as the age of the victim is concerned, there are conflicting materials that have surfaced on the record.
As per the school certificate the victim was 12 years 7 months on the date of the incident.
As per her father, the age of the victim is 16 years.
In statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. the victim has disclosed her age to be 14 years.
No definite basis for recording of age in any of the records has been established by the prosecution.
It is in this context that ossification test has been conducted of the victim in which she has been found to be 18 years of age.

Finding contradiction in the age of the victim as is recorded in school certificate, vis-a-vis the statement of the father and the testimony of the victim, the trial court has found it safe to rely upon the medical evidence to hold that the victim is major.
On this aspect, we have perused the judgement of the trial court, and we find no error in the conclusion arrived at by the trial court.
5. So far as the allegation with regard to the victim being enticed is concerned, the trial court has noticed that the victim has not been consistent at different stages of the proceedings.

She has not supported the prosecution case at the stage of investigation and in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. she has clearly disclosed that it was out of her own volition that she joined the company of the accused.
There has been subsequent improvement when the statement of the victim was recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. wherein she appears to have fallen in line with the prosecution.

At the stage of trial, the victim has, however, supported the prosecution case in its entirety, as per which the victim was told by the accused that he would keep her with him, happily and when she refused the accused tied her face and hands and forcibly abducted.
When she regained consciousness she found that she was traveling in a bus to Delhi.
The victim, however, has admitted that while traveling in the public transport she neither raised any alarm nor made any complaint to anybody.
She remained in a room with the accused for almost a month in Delhi and they formed physical relations on regular basis.

The trial court on the basis of appreciation of the evidence on record has come to the conclusion that the fact that the victim had stayed with the accused without raising any alarm or protest indicates that she had voluntarily joined the company of the accused.
The victim in her initial statement has also taken such stand.
On the basis of the appreciation of material on records, the trial court has,therefore, come to the conclusion that the prosecution has failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond doubt.
With these findings, the trial court has acquitted the accused.

2 6. The court of sessions upon elaborate analysis of the evidence on record has come to the conclusion that prosecution has not been able to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt.
Though learned A.G.A. submits that there is an apparent perversity in the judgment of acquittal, but no such perversity could be substantiated at the time of hearing.

In the circumstances, we find that the view taken by the court of sessions to acquit the accused persons is a permissible view and merely because a different view could have been taken cannot be a ground to interfere with the judgment of acquittal.
Prayer made for grant of leave to challenge the judgment is, therefore, refused.
Consequently, the appeal fails and is dismissed.
